'''Cosmas K. Zachos''' ({{langx|el|Κοσμάς Ζάχος}}; born 1951) is a [[theoretical]] [[physicist]]. He was educated in physics ([[undergraduate]] A.B. 1974) at [[Princeton University]], and did graduate work in theoretical physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Ph.D. 1979 
<ref>Ph.D. dissertation (1979): ''Extended supergravity with a gauged central charge'',  [https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/4718/ online] </ref>) under the supervision of [[John Henry Schwarz]].

Zachos is an emeritus staff member in the theory group of the High Energy Physics Division of [[Argonne National Laboratory]].  He is considered an authority on the subject of [[Phase space formulation|phase-space quantization]].  His early research involved, jointly, the introduction of [[renormalization]] geometrostasis, and the so-called FFZ [[Lie algebra]] of [[noncommutative geometry]]. His thesis work revealed a balancing repulsive gravitational force present in extended [[supergravity]].{{cn|date=August 2026}}

He is co-author of treatises on [[quantum mechanics]] in [[phase space]],<ref>Cosmas K. Zachos, David B. Fairlie, and Thomas L. Curtright, ''Quantum Mechanics in Phase Space''.  (World Scientific,  Singapore, 2005) {{ISBN|978-981-238-384-6}}.</ref><ref>[[Thomas Curtright|Thomas L. Curtright]], [[David Fairlie|David B. Fairlie]], Cosmas K. Zachos, ''A Concise Treatise on Quantum Mechanics in Phase Space'',  (World Scientific,  Singapore, 2014)  {{ISBN|9789814520430}}</ref> a [[List_of_fellows_of_the_American_Physical_Society_(1998–2010)#2010|Fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=cosmas%20zachos&af=true | title=APS Fellows Archive | publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=September 15, 2025}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.anl.gov/hep/awards-recognition|title=Awards & Recognition | publisher=Argonne National Laboratory|access-date=September 26, 2025}}</ref>
